title_en: Huajian Electronics Co., Ltd. and Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd. v. Guangzhou Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd. and Xie Xiongping et al. — dispute over cooperation agreement
ruling_gist_en: For the purpose of reaching cooperation, the parties entered into multiple contracts, but only one of the contracts contained an arbitration clause. After the arbitral award concerning that contract became effective, a lawsuit was filed due to disputes over other contracts that did not contain arbitration clauses. If one party argues that the people's court has no jurisdiction solely on the ground that the arbitral award has already become effective, the people's court shall not support such argument. In circumstances where the contract on which the effective arbitral award is based is different from the contract on which the people's court bases its handling of the dispute, and the content of the people's court's trial does not involve matters covered by the arbitration clause, if one party argues that the people's court should not handle the case again on the ground of res judicata, the people's court shall not support such argument.
keywords_en: Civil; Cooperation agreement dispute; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Guangdong; Legal person; Natural person; Contract Law; Scope of validity of arbitration clause; Application of res judicata principle; Overall relationship of multiple contracts; Reversal of judgment; Cooperation agreement; Equity transfer; Arbitral award; Jurisdictional dispute; Fairness principle; Application for retrial; Jurisdiction; Arbitration; Dispute over cooperation agreement of Xie Xiongping, et al.
full_text_en:
Huajian Electronics Co., Ltd. and Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd. v. Guangzhou Venture Capital Co., Ltd., Xie Xiongping, et al. — dispute over cooperation agreement

[Ruling Summary]

Where parties enter into multiple contracts to achieve a cooperative purpose but only one contract contains an arbitration clause, and after the arbitration award rendered under that contract becomes effective, litigation arises over disputes under other contracts that do not contain an arbitration clause, a party's claim that the people's court lacks jurisdiction solely on the ground that the arbitration award has already become effective shall not be supported by the people's court. Where the contract underlying the effective arbitration award differs from the contract on which the people's court bases its handling of the disputed case, and the content tried by the people's court does not involve matters covered by the arbitration clause, a party's claim that the people's court should not hear the case again on the ground of "res judicata" shall not be supported by the people's court.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2010) Min Ti Zi No. 10

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Huajian Electronics Co., Ltd., domiciled at Kequn Building, No. 30 Xueyuan Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Hong Lin, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yushuang, attorney at Beijing Huicheng Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd., domiciled at West Building, Kequn Building, No. 257 Beisihuan Zhonglu, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Hong Lin, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Yushuang, attorney at Beijing Huicheng Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Guangzhou Venture Capital Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room C204-1, Zone C, Guangzhou International Enterprise Incubator, Science City, Guangzhou High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Feng Mengjue, Chairman of the company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Jicheng, attorney at Guangdong Shenglun Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lu Yuxing, intern attorney at Guangdong Shenglun Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Xie Xiongping, male, Han nationality, born March 8, 1967, residing in Tianhe District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Huang Lisheng, attorney at Guangdong Global Jingwei Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhang Heping, male, Han nationality, born March 15, 1966, registered address: Tianhe District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, current address: Shunde District, Foshan, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Huang Lisheng, attorney at Guangdong Global Jingwei Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Qiu Shaoming, male, Han nationality, born September 12, 1961, registered address: Yuexiu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, current address: Guangzhou High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Guangdong Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Huang Ruohao, male, Han nationality, born May 25, 1962, registered address: collective household of Tianjin High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Shipai Section, Zhongshan Avenue, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province, current address: Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

With respect to the dispute over a cooperation agreement between the applicants for retrial, Huajian Electronics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huajian Electronics) and Huajian Machine Translation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huajian Translation), and the respondents, Guangzhou Venture Capital Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Venture Capital Company), Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, the Guangdong High People's Court rendered Civil Ruling (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315 on June 3, 2008, which has become legally effective. This Court rendered Civil Ruling (2008) Min Shen Zi No. 833 on July 20, 2009, deciding to retry this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing on May 13, 2010. Wang Yushuang, agent ad litem for Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation; Liu Jicheng and Lu Yuxing, agents ad litem for Venture Capital Company; and Huang Lisheng, agent ad litem for Xie Xiongping and Zhang Heping, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. Qiu Shaoming and Huang Ruohao, after being lawfully summoned by this Court, did not appear in court. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

On August 8, 2006, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation filed a lawsuit with the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, alleging that in the second half of 2004, due to the unsatisfactory performance of Guangzhou Kuangshi Technology Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kuangshi Company) and the downturn in the Hong Kong stock market, the overseas subsidiary listing process of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation was stalled. After various considerations, in early 2005, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation reached a consensus with Venture Capital Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao that a near-term listing was difficult, and they agreed, in accordance with the provisions of the "Cooperation Agreement," to terminate the three agreements already signed, namely the "Cooperation Agreement," the "Equity Transfer Agreement," and the "Framework Agreement" for introducing venture investors from Huajian Electronics, and to restore Kuangshi Company to its original state. However, Venture Capital Company repeatedly delayed handling the industrial and commercial registration procedures for restoring the equity of Kuangshi Company on various pretexts. At the end of 2005, Venture Capital Company, disregarding the already reached agreement on terminating the cooperation and restoring the equity structure, took advantage of the current status of Kuangshi Company's equity registration that had not yet been restored and, unilaterally relying on the "Equity Transfer Agreement," applied for arbitration. Since the arbitration clause was only stipulated in the "Equity Transfer Agreement," and Venture Capital Company refused to reach an arbitration agreement regarding the "Cooperation Agreement" and the "Framework Agreement" as part of an overall cooperative project, this ultimately led to the Beijing Arbitration Commission's award that Huajian Electronics should bear the adverse consequence of paying equity transfer consideration and interest. According to Article 3, Item 15 of the "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, Venture Capital Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, if for various reasons Huajian Electronics' restructuring and listing fails, then this Agreement, the "Equity Transfer Agreement," and the "Framework Agreement" shall be terminated. For the part already performed, the parties agree to restore the original state as much as possible, including (but not limited to) returning the agreement price, restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company, and re-making corresponding industrial and commercial changes. For losses caused to both parties thereby, the parties agree to bear them respectively in accordance with the principle of fairness. By severing the overall relationship among the "Cooperation Agreement," the "Framework Agreement," and the "Equity Transfer Agreement," concealing the true background of the equity transfer, and applying for arbitration, Venture Capital Company seriously violated the provisions of Article 3, Item 15 of the "Cooperation Agreement." This act directly compelled Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation to initiate this lawsuit to restore the facts and protect their legitimate rights and interests, causing severe economic losses to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation. They requested the people's court: 1. To confirm that the "Cooperation Agreement" is lawful and effective; 2. To order the termination of the "Cooperation Agreement," and to register the change of 90% of Kuangshi Company's equity nominally held by Huajian Electronics to be held by Xie Xiongping (36.11%), Huang Ruohao (14.33%), Zhang Heping (14.31%), Qiu Shaoming (0.25%), and Venture Capital Company (25%), and to register the change of 10% of Kuangshi Company's equity nominally held by Huajian Translation to be held by Xie Xiongping; 3. To order Venture Capital Company to compensate Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation for additional economic losses of RMB 166,435.3 caused by Venture Capital Company's breach of contract, including arbitration attorney fees of RMB 50,000, funds of RMB 48,000 already deducted in the enforcement of the arbitration award by the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, arbitration fees of RMB 51,630 borne by Huajian Electronics, and expenses of RMB 16,805.3 for traveling to Guangzhou for investigation and evidence collection; 4. To have Venture Capital Company bear the litigation costs of this case.

Venture Capital Company argued in its defense that the "Cooperation Agreement" was the true expression of the parties' intentions and was lawful and effective, but the "Cooperation Agreement" was not actually performed. It was merely an expression of intent for cooperation between the parties and was not specifically binding on the parties. Venture Capital Company disagreed with the second claim of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation. It did not request the termination of the "Cooperation Agreement," so Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation had no basis to request Venture Capital Company to perform under Article 3, Item 15 of the "Cooperation Agreement." Without terminating the "Equity Transfer Agreement," the second claim raised by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation could not be established.

Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, and Qiu Shaoming jointly argued in their defense at first instance that they agreed with Venture Capital Company's defense, i.e., the "Cooperation Agreement" was merely a letter of intent between the parties, and it was not actually performed. What was actually performed was the "Equity Transfer Agreement." Regardless of whether the "Cooperation Agreement" was lawful and effective, it had no connection with changing the equity structure. Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation alleged that they did not participate in the business planning, but the directors of Kuangshi Company were all appointed by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province found that on December 25, 2003, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation jointly as Party A and Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Venture Capital Company jointly as Party B signed a "Cooperation Agreement" stipulating that Parties A and B reached a cooperation intention regarding equity transfer and investment. Party A intended to acquire all equity of Kuangshi Company held by Party B, and at the same time, Party B intended to act as a venture investor in Party A's overseas proposed listed company. Party A promised that Party B's affiliated companies could obtain shares of Party A's subsidiary to be listed on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong in accordance with the terms of the "Framework Agreement." For the needs of Party A's listing work, Party B agreed that after the signing of this Agreement, it would begin to make industrial and commercial changes to Kuangshi Company as required by Party A, but Party A promised that until the listing, the actual controller of Kuangshi Company would still be Party B, and its actual owner's equity would not be changed before the listing. If for various reasons Party A's restructuring and listing failed, then this Agreement, the "Equity Transfer Agreement," and the "Framework Agreement" would be terminated. For the part already performed, the parties agreed to restore the original state as much as possible, including (but not limited to) returning the agreement price, restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company, and re-making corresponding industrial and commercial registration changes. For losses caused to both parties thereby, the parties agreed to bear them respectively in accordance with the principle of fairness.

On the same day the above agreement was signed, Huajian Electronics as Party A and Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Huang Ruohao, Qiu Shaoming, and Venture Capital Company as Party B signed a "Framework Agreement" for introducing venture investors from Huajian Electronics, stipulating that Party A intended to restructure its business and list on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong. Party A guaranteed that after the share transfer, Party B would undergo equity conversion, i.e., after the equity conversion, Party B would own 8% of the equity of Huajian (Cayman), but the final equity ratio of Party B in Huajian (Cayman) would be determined by the total market value of the company at the time of its public offering and the market value available for Party B to subscribe as finally confirmed by Parties A and B. The per-share transfer price for Parties A and B would be the issue price when Huajian (Cayman) was listed on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong. Party A guaranteed that Huajian (Cayman) would be listed on the Growth Enterprise Market of Hong Kong. If for various reasons the listing failed, then the "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Parties A and B would be terminated, and all payments already made by Party B would be returned in the manner provided in the "Cooperation Agreement."

On the same day the above two agreements were signed, Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Venture Capital Company jointly as Party A and Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation jointly as Party B signed an "Equity Transfer Agreement," stipulating that Party A would transfer 95% of its equity in Kuangshi Company to Party B, including Venture Capital Company transferring all of its 25% equity in Kuangshi Company to Huajian Electronics. Any disputes would be submitted to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for resolution. Given that the registered capital of Kuangshi Company was RMB 12 million, the amount of registered capital transferred by Venture Capital Company to Huajian Electronics was RMB 3 million. After the above equity transfer, the shareholding structure of Kuangshi Company was: Xie Xiongping's capital contribution was RMB 600,000, accounting for 5% of the registered capital; Huajian Electronics' capital contribution was RMB 10.8 million, accounting for 90%; Huajian Translation's capital contribution was RMB 600,000, accounting for 5%. The parties lawfully handled the equity change registration. On February 2, 2004, Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, and Xie Xiongping held a shareholders' meeting, deciding to approve Xie Xiongping's transfer of his 5% capital contribution of RMB 600,000 to Huajian Translation, and handled the industrial and commercial change registration procedures.

On February 5, 2003, the China Securities Regulatory Commission approved and agreed to accept the application for the restructuring and overseas listing of Huajian Electronics by a document [2001] No. 112, and required the company to expedite preparations and fulfill relevant approval procedures in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and rules.

In the second half of 2004, due to various considerations such as company performance and listing timing, the listing process was delayed to a certain extent. In early 2005, after various considerations, Huajian Electronics reached a consensus with the original shareholders of Kuangshi Company that a near-term listing was difficult, and they agreed to rescind the signed agreements and sign corresponding termination agreements to restore Kuangshi Company to its original state. In mid-March 2005, Kuangshi Company held a board of directors' meeting (i.e., original shareholders and shareholder representatives) to collectively discuss matters of restoring Kuangshi Company's equity structure. At that time, representatives of Venture Capital Company, Yang Lin and Shen Kun, also attended the meeting. After consultation and consensus, all agreed on the restoration matters and decided that Kuangshi Company would send a letter to Huajian Electronics requesting cooperation in handling industrial and commercial change procedures. On April 30, 2005, Huajian Electronics sent a draft termination agreement and corresponding documents to Huang Ruohao via email. On February 13, 2006, Huang Ruohao and Zhang Heping issued a statement and letter of guarantee to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, stating that regardless of whether the "Cooperation Agreement," the "Framework Agreement," and the "Equity Transfer Agreement" (including 95%, 100%, and 5% equity transfers) signed in December 2003 by Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, Xie Xiongping, Venture Capital Company, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, and Qiu Shaoming were valid, they declared that as of February 13, 2006, they would terminate the performance of these three agreements, and at the same time, they guaranteed that they would not assert against Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation any obligation to perform any obligations stipulated in these three agreements. Xie Xiongping also issued a letter of guarantee to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, stating that they guaranteed that they would not assert against Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation any obligation to perform any obligations stipulated in these three agreements.

On December 12, 2005, Venture Capital Company applied for arbitration with the Beijing Arbitration Commission based on the arbitration clause in the "Equity Transfer Agreement," requesting a ruling that Huajian Electronics pay equity transfer consideration of RMB 3 million and interest. After hearing the case, the arbitration tribunal held that since the "Framework Agreement" and the "Cooperation Agreement" did not stipulate that relevant disputes between the parties would be submitted to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for arbitration, the arbitration tribunal had suggested that the parties consider submitting the disputes under the "Framework Agreement" and the "Cooperation Agreement" to the arbitration tribunal for joint hearing, but the parties failed to reach a consensus on this. Accordingly, the arbitration tribunal declined to hear any disputes that might exist between the parties based on the "Framework Agreement" and the "Cooperation Agreement." The arbitration tribunal also pointed out that Article 125 of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract Law") provides that the purpose of the contract should be considered when interpreting it, but given the existence of agreed arbitration rules, even if the arbitration tribunal discovered that there were other complex commercial purposes when the parties signed the "Equity Transfer Agreement," the arbitration tribunal had no authority to make an ultra vires ruling solely based on the purpose of the contract. Consequently, on May 16, 2006, it rendered the (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 award, with the following content: 1. Huajian Electronics shall pay Venture Capital Company equity transfer fee of RMB 3 million; 2. Huajian Electronics shall pay Venture Capital Company overdue payment interest of RMB 440,000 and overdue payment interest from December 1, 2005, until the date of full payment of the equity transfer consideration (calculated at 0.021% per day). Venture Capital Company applied for compulsory enforcement based on the (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 award with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, which lawfully deducted RMB 48,000 from Huajian Electronics.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province held that the "Cooperation Agreement" signed by Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, and Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Venture Capital Company was the true expression of the parties' intentions, and its contents did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, making it a valid agreement. The parties should strictly perform their respective obligations in accordance with the agreement. The agreement stipulated: "If for various reasons Party A's restructuring and listing fails, then this Agreement, the Equity Transfer Agreement signed by the parties, and the VC Investment Agreement shall be terminated. For the part already performed, the parties agree to restore the original state as much as possible, including (but not limited to) returning the agreement price, restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company, and re-making corresponding industrial and commercial changes. For losses caused to both parties thereby, the parties agree to bear them respectively in accordance with the principle of fairness." After the signing of the "Cooperation Agreement," Huajian Electronics, in accordance with the agreement, registered the change of Xie Xiongping's 46.11% equity in Kuangshi Company, Huang Ruohao's 14.33%, Zhang Heping's 14.31%, Qiu Shaoming's 0.25%, and Venture Capital Company's 25% equity to be held by Huajian Electronics (90%) and Huajian Translation (10%). Huajian Electronics signed the above agreements and handled the equity change registration for the purpose of fulfilling the requirements of the China Securities Regulatory Commission to expedite preparations and fulfill relevant approval procedures. Due to various reasons such as company performance and listing timing, Huajian Electronics' indirect overseas listing was not completed. With respect to the failure to list, Huajian Electronics had notified the original shareholders of Kuangshi Company and requested the termination of the "Cooperation Agreement." Venture Capital Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao failed to assist Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation in performing the industrial and commercial change registration obligations in accordance with the agreement to restore the equity of Kuangshi Company to its original state. Their actions constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding liability for breach. Therefore, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation's request, based on Venture Capital Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao's failure to perform the obligations under the "Cooperation Agreement," to register the change of the 90% and 10% equity they each held in Kuangshi Company to be held by Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Venture Capital Company should be supported.

The Equity Transfer Agreement signed by Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao contained an arbitration clause, and an arbitral award was rendered by the Beijing Arbitration Commission, which has become legally effective. Since Huajian Electronics must transfer its 25% equity in Kuangshi Company to Technology Company's name, Technology Company obtained RMB 48,000 in equity transfer payments without legal basis, and Technology Company should return this amount to Huajian Electronics. Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation claimed that Technology Company's breach caused them additional economic losses, including arbitration attorney fees of RMB 50,000, arbitration costs of RMB 51,630 payable by Huajian Electronics, and RMB 16,805.3 for travel to Guangzhou to investigate and collect evidence, totaling RMB 118,435.3. Because the above losses had no necessary causal relationship with this case, the claim by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation for compensation for these losses cannot be sustained and is not supported. The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court rendered civil judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220 on August 23, 2007: (1) The Cooperation Agreement signed in December 2003 between Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company is dissolved. (2) Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company shall, within one month from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, assist Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation in transferring the 90% and 10% equity interests in Kuangshi Company held by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, respectively, to the names of Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, to be held by Xie Xiongping (46.11%), Huang Ruohao (14.33%), Zhang Heping (14.31%), Qiu Shaoming (0.25%), and Technology Company (25%). (3) Technology Company shall, within ten days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, return RMB 48,000 to Huajian Electronics. (4) The other claims of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation are dismissed. Court acceptance fees of RMB 70,842 shall be borne jointly by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation in the amount of RMB 690; and by Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company in proportion to their respective shareholdings in the amount of RMB 70,152.

Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, and Qiu Shaoming, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, arguing: 1. The termination condition stipulated in the Cooperation Agreement is not a true condition. The first-instance judgment's determination that the condition was fulfilled lacked sufficient basis, and ruling to dissolve the Cooperation Agreement had no factual basis. 2. The first-instance judgment ignored the effective arbitral award. Without the Equity Transfer Agreement being dissolved, revoked, or declared invalid, the judgment directly ordered the restoration of equity, seriously violating the principle of ne bis in idem. If this judgment becomes effective, it will result in a serious conflict with the arbitral award, undermining judicial authority. Terminating the Cooperation Agreement cannot produce the legal consequence of restoring the equity ratio. The first-instance judgment's order to restore equity had no legal basis. The award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 rendered by the Beijing Arbitration Commission had already found the following facts: the actual performance was the Equity Transfer Agreement (transfer of 95% of the equity), which was legally valid, and Technology Company had the right to demand continued performance, i.e., the right to demand that Huajian Electronics pay RMB 3 million in equity transfer payments and liquidated damages. Huajian Electronics' application to the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court to set aside the arbitral award had been dismissed. However, in this case, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation's claim was to terminate the Cooperation Agreement and restore the equity. According to Article 3, Paragraph 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, only if the Cooperation Agreement, the Equity Transfer Agreement, and the Framework Agreement are terminated simultaneously would the legal consequence of equity restoration arise, rather than being a consequence of performing the Cooperation Agreement. The Cooperation Agreement itself did not address the specific matters of equity transfer. Merely terminating the Cooperation Agreement could not produce the legal consequence of restoring the equity ratio. The first-instance court, in its judgment, did not address the Equity Transfer Agreement (transfer of 95% of the equity) or declare it invalid, yet directly ordered the restoration of the equity ratio and required Technology Company to return funds obtained under the effective arbitral award. This was a completely erroneous judgment.

Zhang Heping, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed, arguing: 1. The first-instance judgment severed the connections among the Cooperation Agreement, the Equity Transfer Agreement, and the Shareholder Transfer of Capital Contribution Contract. The claims of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation were to terminate the Cooperation Agreement and transfer the 36.11% equity in Huajian Electronics' name and the 10% equity in Huajian Translation's name to Zhang Heping. However, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation did not simultaneously request the dissolution of the Equity Transfer Agreement and the Shareholder Transfer of Capital Contribution Contract. The Cooperation Agreement was merely a letter of intent for cooperation between Zhang Heping and Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation; the specific rights and obligations were set forth in the Equity Transfer Agreement and the Shareholder Transfer of Capital Contribution Contract signed by the parties. The document registered and filed with the administrative department for industry and commerce was the Shareholder Transfer of Capital Contribution Contract, not the Cooperation Agreement. In 2003 and 2004, Zhang Heping transferred his 46.11% equity interest in the company involved to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation pursuant to the Shareholder Transfer of Capital Contribution Contract signed with them. Since Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation did not request the dissolution of the Equity Transfer Agreement and the Shareholder Transfer of Capital Contribution Contract, the equity could not be returned to Zhang Heping under the Cooperation Agreement. 2. The first-instance judgment applied the law improperly, cited legal provisions that contradicted each other, and its decision exceeded the claims of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation. Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation requested termination of the Cooperation Agreement, not dissolution. The first-instance judgment exceeded their claims. 3. The award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 rendered and effective by the Beijing Arbitration Commission ruled that Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation should pay RMB 3 million in equity transfer payments to Technology Company. This award had become effective and had been enforced. However, the first-instance judgment used its decision to overturn the said arbitral award, seriously violating the law. In summary, the first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and improperly applied the law. Zhang Heping requested that the appellate court set aside items 1 and 2 of the first-instance judgment and dismiss the claims of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation.

Xie Xiongping and Qiu Shaoming were also dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment and filed an appeal. Their appellate requests and grounds were the same as those of Zhang Heping.

Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation jointly responded in the second instance, arguing that the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law. The appeals of Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Zhang Heping had no basis, and they requested that the appellate court dismiss their appellate requests.

The Guangdong High People's Court, upon further investigation, found that the facts found by the first-instance court were substantially accurate and confirmed them.

Separately found: In December 2003, Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, Huang Ruohao, Huajian Electronics, and Huajian Translation signed the Equity Transfer Agreement, stipulating that Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao would transfer all of their equity in Kuangshi Company to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, and Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation would pay RMB 12 million in equity transfer fees to Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao.

Huajian Electronics, believing that the award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474 rendered by the Beijing Arbitration Commission had erroneous findings of fact, applied to the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court to set aside the said award. The Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, on October 27, 2006, rendered civil ruling (2006) Er Zhong Min Te Zi No. 12426, dismissing Huajian Electronics' application to set aside the arbitral award.

The Guangdong High People's Court held that Huajian Electronics, Huajian Translation, Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao signed the Cooperation Agreement, the Framework Agreement, and the Equity Transfer Agreement regarding the equity transfer of Kuangshi Company. The above agreements were all true expressions of the parties' intentions, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, and the equity in Kuangshi Company had already been transferred to the names of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation. Therefore, the above contracts were all valid and legally binding on the parties involved.

After the above contracts were signed, Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, in accordance with the contract terms, transferred their equity in Kuangshi Company to Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation and registered the relevant equity in their names. On December 12, 2005, Technology Company applied to the Beijing Arbitration Commission for arbitration, alleging that Huajian Electronics had breached the Equity Transfer Agreement by failing to pay the equity transfer price. On May 16, 2006, the Beijing Arbitration Commission rendered award (2006) Jing Zhong Cai Zi No. 0474, ruling that Huajian Electronics should pay Technology Company RMB 3 million in equity transfer fees, RMB 440,000 in overdue interest, and overdue interest from December 1, 2005, until full payment of the equity transfer price. Huajian Electronics, dissatisfied with the arbitral award, filed an application with the Beijing No. 2 Intermediate People's Court to set aside the award, which was dismissed. Now, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation, based on the Cooperation Agreement, filed a lawsuit in the people's court against Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, requesting termination of the Cooperation Agreement and transfer of the equity in Kuangshi Company to the names of Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao. Although the parties stipulated in the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement that if Huajian Electronics' overseas subsidiary failed to be listed in Hong Kong, then the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement should be terminated and the equity in Kuangshi Company should be restored to the names of Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao, the arbitral body did not adjudicate on the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement. In this case, the Cooperation Agreement, the Framework Agreement, and the Equity Transfer Agreement constitute an inseparable whole, and the people's court should have tried the above agreements together. Since the arbitral body, based on the Equity Transfer Agreement, had already ruled that Huajian Electronics should pay Technology Company RMB 3 million in equity transfer fees and overdue interest, the acceptance by the people's court of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation's claim to terminate the Cooperation Agreement and transfer the equity in Kuangshi Company to the names of Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao necessarily involved the Equity Transfer Agreement. Since the arbitral body had already rendered a decision on the Equity Transfer Agreement, the claims of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation would inevitably conflict with the arbitral award. The first-instance court's decision to dissolve the Cooperation Agreement and restore the equity in Kuangshi Company held by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation to the names of Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao contradicted the content of the relevant arbitral award. This essentially re-adjudicated the matter already decided by the arbitral body, violating the principle of ne bis in idem. The first-instance court's acceptance of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation's lawsuit and its rendering of a substantive judgment were improper and are hereby corrected according to law. On June 3, 2008, the Guangdong High People's Court rendered civil ruling (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315: Set aside the civil judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court; Dismiss the lawsuit of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation. Court acceptance fees of RMB 50 for each instance are borne by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation.

Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation applied for retrial pursuant to Article 179, Paragraph 1, Item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), requesting the revocation of civil ruling (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315 of the Guangdong High People's Court and the affirmation of civil judgment (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220 of the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court. The main reasons are as follows:

(A) The lawsuit filed by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation met the conditions prescribed by law, and the two contracts on which the lawsuit was based did not contain an arbitration clause. The people's court should have accepted the case and conducted substantive trial. The Guangdong High People's Court's dismissal of the lawsuit of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation based on Article 111, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law was an erroneous application of law.

(B) The trial of this case by the people's court did not conflict with the award of the Beijing Arbitration Commission. The dispute among the parties regarding the restoration of the equity structure of Kuangshi Company under the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement, and the dispute among the parties regarding the payment of equity transfer fees for Kuangshi Company under the Equity Transfer Agreement, are different legal relationships. They do not fall within the circumstances prescribed by the principle of ne bis in idem. The Guangdong High People's Court's application of this principle in the second-instance ruling was clearly an erroneous application of law.

(C) The lawsuit filed by Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation based on the valid Cooperation Agreement and Framework Agreement was dismissed by the people's court, and the arbitral tribunal, when trying the Equity Transfer Agreement, did not address the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement. This left no avenue for protecting the legitimate rights and interests of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation.

Technology Company responded, arguing that the people's court indeed has the authority to try the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement. However, since the termination condition stipulated in the Cooperation Agreement in this case is not fulfilled, the people's court cannot determine that the Cooperation Agreement and related agreements should be terminated on this basis, nor can it directly render a decision to restore the equity structure.

Xie Xiongping and Zhang Heping responded, arguing that although the people's court has jurisdiction over the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Investment Agreement, if the people's court determines that Article 3, Paragraph 15 of the Cooperation Agreement is a valid stipulation, then the decision would inevitably conflict with the effective arbitral award, violating the principle of ne bis in idem.

The facts found upon retrial by this Court are the same as those found by the courts of first and second instance.

This Court holds that, based on the reasons for the parties' application for retrial and the responses, the issues in dispute in this case are as follows.

I. Whether this case falls within the jurisdiction of the people's court.

The Guangdong High People's Court dismissed the lawsuit of Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation based on Article 111, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law. In their application for retrial, Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation argued that the two contracts on which they based their lawsuit did not contain an arbitration clause, and the people's court should have accepted the case and conducted substantive trial. After this Court held a hearing, the respondents Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, and Zhang Heping also believed that the people's court has jurisdiction over this case.

This Court holds that the basis for Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation to file this lawsuit is the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement, and these two agreements do not contain an arbitration clause. The arbitral award explicitly stated: "The arbitral tribunal will not try the disputes that may exist between the parties based on the Framework Agreement and the Cooperation Agreement." Accordingly, this case falls within the jurisdiction of the people's court. The Guangdong High People's Court's determination, based on Article 111, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law, that this case does not fall within the jurisdiction of the people's court, was an erroneous application of law. This Court hereby corrects it according to law.

II. Whether the stipulation in Article 3, Paragraph 15 of the Cooperation Agreement is invalid, and whether the termination condition stipulated therein is fulfilled.

Technology Company argued that the stipulation in Article 3, Paragraph 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, that "if for any reason Party A's restructuring and listing are unsuccessful, then this agreement, the equity transfer agreement signed by the parties, and the VC investment agreement shall be terminated," should be considered a conditional termination clause, but the attached condition "if for any reason Party A's restructuring and listing are unsuccessful" is not a true condition, and this stipulation is invalid. Huajian Electronics and Huajian Translation argued that this stipulation does not violate mandatory provisions of law and should be valid.

This Court holds that the basis for determining that a contract or a condition stipulated in a contract is invalid is the provisions of Article 52 of the Contract Law. The condition stipulated in Article 3, Paragraph 15 of the Cooperation Agreement does not violate the provisions of Article 52 of the Contract Law regarding the invalidity of contracts, and should be determined valid according to law. Since the contract is valid, it should be strictly performed in accordance with the content of Article 3, Paragraph 15 of the Cooperation Agreement. If the condition "if for any reason Party A's restructuring and listing are unsuccessful" has been fulfilled, then "this agreement, the equity transfer agreement signed by the parties, and the VC investment agreement shall be terminated." In this case, although a series of operations were carried out by the parties, particularly Huajian Electronics, the objective fact is that Huajian Electronics' overseas subsidiary ultimately failed to be listed in Hong Kong, which is consistent with the parties' stipulation, i.e., "if for any reason Party A's restructuring and listing are unsuccessful." Therefore, the condition for terminating the Cooperation Agreement and other contracts has been fulfilled. Consequently, the first-instance court's finding that "Huajian Electronics had notified the original shareholders of Kuangshi Company of the failed listing and requested termination of the Cooperation Agreement. The five defendants failed to assist the two plaintiffs in performing the industrial and commercial registration changes to restore the equity of Kuangshi Company to its original state, and their actions constituted a breach of contract, for which they should bear corresponding liability for breach. Therefore, the two plaintiffs' claim, based on the five defendants' failure to perform their obligations under the Cooperation Agreement, to completely transfer the 90% and 10% equity interests they respectively hold in Kuangshi Company to the names of the defendants Xie Xiongping, Huang Ruohao, Zhang Heping, Qiu Shaoming, and Technology Company, is supported by this Court," is consistent with the parties' agreement and legal provisions. This Court hereby affirms it according to law. Pursuant to the Cooperation Agreement, the parties are to restore the performed Equity Transfer Agreement to its original state. Huajian Electronics shall return its 25% equity in Kuangshi Company to Technology Company, and Technology Company shall return the consideration received for the transfer of that equity, including RMB 48,000, to Huajian Electronics.

III. Whether the first-instance court's decision to restore the equity to its original state violates the principle of ne bis in idem and conflicts with the arbitral award.

Technology Company, Xie Xiongping, and Zhang Heping all argued that the arbitral award had already ruled: 1. Huajian Electronics Company shall pay Technology Company RMB 3,000,000 as equity transfer consideration; 2. Huajian Electronics Company shall pay Technology Company overdue payment interest of RMB 440,000 and overdue payment interest from December 1, 2005 until the date the equity transfer consideration is fully paid off (calculated at 2.1 parts per ten thousand per day). If the people's court further ruled to restore the equity to its original state, it would violate the principle of res judicata and contradict the arbitral award. Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company argued that the dispute among the parties concerning the restoration of Kuangshi Company's equity structure to its original state under the Cooperation Agreement and the Framework Agreement, and the dispute concerning the payment of equity transfer consideration for Kuangshi Company under the Equity Transfer Agreement, were different legal relationships and did not constitute a situation governed by the principle of res judicata. Therefore, the people's court's trial of this case did not conflict with the arbitral award rendered by the Beijing Arbitration Commission.

This Court holds that the first-instance court's judgment restoring the equity to its original state did not violate the principle of res judicata. The reasons are as follows: Because "restructuring and listing was not achieved," the dispute in which Huajian Electronics Company and Huajian Translation Company requested, based on Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, the restoration of Kuangshi Company's equity structure to its original state, and the dispute concerning the payment of equity transfer consideration for Kuangshi Company under the Equity Transfer Agreement, are different legal relationships. These are different requests made by the parties based on different legal facts. From the provisions of the Cooperation Agreement, the performance of that agreement is divided into two stages. The first stage is to carry out the transfer of Kuangshi Company's equity and pay the equity transfer consideration in order to achieve the successful restructuring and listing of Huajian Electronics Company's overseas subsidiaries. The second stage is that if the "restructuring and listing is not achieved," then restore the equity structure of Kuangshi Company and return the transfer consideration. To perform the matters agreed upon for the first stage, the parties further executed the Equity Transfer Agreement, which contained an arbitration clause, excluding the jurisdiction of the people's court. That dispute has already been arbitrated by the Beijing Arbitration Commission. However, for the performance of the matters agreed upon for the second stage, namely, "if Party A's restructuring and listing is not achieved due to various reasons, then this agreement, the equity transfer agreement signed by both parties, and the VC investment agreement shall be terminated. For the parts that have been performed, the parties agree to restore the original state as far as possible, including but not limited to returning the agreement price, restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Technology, re-conducting corresponding industrial and commercial changes, etc. For the losses caused to the parties thereby, the parties agree to bear them respectively according to the principle of fairness." Huajian Electronics Company filed this lawsuit based on that provision. This case resolves precisely the dispute arising from the performance of the second stage of the Cooperation Agreement. Because the basis on which the first-instance court handled this case was not the Equity Transfer Agreement, but rather Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement, while the arbitration was based on the Equity Transfer Agreement, not on Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement. Since the agreement underlying the arbitral award is different from the agreement on which the first-instance court based its decision in this case, that is, the first-instance court did not adjudicate the dispute arising from the performance of the Equity Transfer Agreement. The arbitral award also expressly stated that it would not include the Cooperation Agreement within the scope of arbitration. In other words, the "same matter" adjudicated in the arbitral award, i.e., the dispute under the Equity Transfer Agreement, was not adjudicated by the people's court. Therefore, the first-instance court's judgment restoring the equity to its original state did not violate the principle of res judicata.

Given that the first-instance court's judgment restoring the equity to its original state did not violate the principle of res judicata, the question of whether the judgment contradicts the arbitral award does not arise. Even if the result of the arbitral award is to perform the Equity Transfer Agreement, while the result of the judgment is to restore the equity structure of Kuangshi Company, the judgment was made based on the provisions of Article 3, Item 15 of the Cooperation Agreement. That provision remains the true expression of intent of all parties, including Technology Company, Zhang Heping, Xie Xiongping, Qiu Shaoming, and Huang Ruohao. In other words, both the first-instance judgment and the arbitral award were made based on the true expression of the parties' intent, and both are necessary results of the parties' performance of their agreements. Stated differently, the true intention of the parties was that, in order to achieve the restructuring and listing, the equity change of Kuangshi Company should first be carried out, and in fact the equity change was carried out. However, if the listing is not achieved, the changed equity should be restored to its original state. Given that the listing was not achieved, the first-instance court's judgment restoring the equity structure of Kuangshi Company should be sustained according to law.

In summary, pursuant to Article 186, paragraph 1, and Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the civil ruling No. (2007) Yue Gao Fa Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 315 of the Guangdong High People's Court.

2. Affirm the civil judgment No. (2006) Sui Zhong Fa Min Er Chu Zi No. 220 of the Intermediate People's Court of Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

This judgment is final.
